$$
\int_{0}^{\sqrt{\ln{\left(2 \right)}}} 2 x e^{2 x^{2} + 1}\,\mathrm{d}x
$$

Choose the exact value."] [:db/add "24bdcdaf-ab24-5eb7-9897-4aa4058292eb" :question/worked-solution "Let $u=2 x^{2} + 1$. Then $\mathrm{d}u=(4 x)\,\mathrm{d}x$.

Transform both bounds:

$$
\begin{aligned}x=0&\Longrightarrow u=1\\x=\sqrt{\ln{\left(2 \right)}}&\Longrightarrow u=1 + \ln{\left(4 \right)}\end{aligned}
$$

Including the differential factor gives

$$
\begin{aligned}&\int_{0}^{\sqrt{\ln{\left(2 \right)}}} 2 x e^{2 x^{2} + 1}\,\mathrm{d}x\\&=\frac{1}{2}\left(\int_{1}^{1 + \ln{\left(4 \right)}} e^{u}\,\mathrm{d}u\right).\end{aligned}
$$

Endpoint values: $e^{\ln 2}=2,\quad e^{2\ln 2}=4$.

Use the integration rule:

$$
\int e^{u}\,\mathrm{d}u=e^{u}+C.
$$

Evaluate the primitive and subtract lower from upper:

$$
\frac{1}{2}\left(\left[e^{u}\right]_{1}^{1 + \ln{\left(4 \right)}}\right)=\frac{1}{2}\left(\left(4 e\right)-\left(e\right)\right).
$$

The exact answer is

$$
\frac{3 e}{2}.
$$"] [:db/add "24bdcdaf-ab24-5eb7-9897-4aa4058292eb" :question/difficulty :question.difficulty/easy] [:db/add "24bdcdaf-ab24-5eb7-9897-4aa4058292eb" :question/answer-fields $$
\begin{aligned}x=0&\Longrightarrow u=1\\x=\sqrt{\ln{\left(2 \right)}}&\Longrightarrow u=\ln{\left(2 \right)} + 1\end{aligned}

$$
\begin{aligned}&\int_{0}^{\sqrt{\ln{\left(2 \right)}}} x e^{x^{2} + 1}\,\mathrm{d}x\\&=\frac{1}{2}\left(\int_{1}^{\ln{\left(2 \right)} + 1} e^{u}\,\mathrm{d}u\right).\end{aligned}

Endpoint values: $e^{\ln 2}=2,\quad e^{2\ln 2}=4$.

Use the integration rule:

$$
\int e^{u}\,\mathrm{d}u=e^{u}+C.
$$

Evaluate the primitive and subtract lower from upper:

$$
\frac{1}{2}\left(\left[e^{u}\right]_{1}^{\ln{\left(2 \right)} + 1}\right)=\frac{1}{2}\left(\left(2 e\right)-\left(e\right)\right).
$$

\frac{e}{2}.
